Roast Pork for Saturnalia

Served at: Saturnalia

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Roast pork was a central dish in the ancient Roman festival of Saturnalia, a celebration honoring the god Saturn. This festive meal symbolized abundance and goodwill, traditionally enjoyed with family and friends during the winter solstice festivities.

Ingredients

  • 4 lb (1.8 kg) pork shoulder or pork loin roast, bone-in
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tbsp fresh rosemary, chopped
  • 1 tbsp fresh thyme, chopped
  • 1 tbsp fennel seeds
  • 1 tsp ground black pepper
  • 1 tbsp kosher salt
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dry white wine or apple cider
  • 1 cup (240 ml) chicken broth

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, fennel seeds, black pepper, and salt to form a herb paste.
  3. Rub the herb mixture all over the pork roast, ensuring it is evenly coated.
  4. Place the pork roast on a rack in a roasting pan.
  5. Pour the white wine (or apple cider) and chicken broth into the bottom of the pan to keep the meat moist during roasting.
  6. Roast the pork in the preheated oven for about 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C).
  7. Baste the pork occasionally with the pan juices to enhance flavor and moisture.
  8. Once cooked, remove the roast from the oven and let it rest for 15 minutes before slicing.
  9. Serve the roast pork with the pan juices spooned over the top.

Tips

  • For a crispier skin, score the fat on top of the pork before applying the herb rub.
  • If fresh herbs are unavailable, use 1 teaspoon each of dried rosemary and thyme instead.
  • Serve with seasonal root vegetables or a simple green salad to complement the rich flavors.
